title: Kushite conquest of Egypt under Piye
summary: Piye, a king of Kush ruling from Napata, conquered Upper Egypt and founded the Twenty-fifth Dynasty of Kushite pharaohs. His victory stela, dated c. 725 BCE, records a campaign against Tefnakht, who had seized the west and sailed southward, and Piye sailing north to Memphis. Egypt had been divided among rival rulers in the Third Intermediate Period.

uncertainty.note: Sources do not give one date for the conquest. EBSCO gives Piye r. 742-716 B.C.E. and BlackPast 743 to 712 BC; the Attalus translation dates the victory stela c. 725 B.C. (regnal year 21). Start is the 742 BCE accession year (astronomical -741); end is c. 725 BCE (-724). Conversions use year = 1 - BCE.

where.historical_name: Memphis, Egypt, in the Third Intermediate Period when rival rulers divided the country

importance.justification: A Nubian kingdom took control of Egypt and ruled it as the Twenty-fifth Dynasty, linking the Nile Valley under Kushite kings.

reviewer_note: Least sure of the date: the opened sources give Piye's reign as 742-716 and 743-712 BCE and the stela as c. 725 BCE, and none dates the conquest itself, so the range runs from accession to the stela. Pin is Memphis (the stela has the king sailing north to Memphis); Napata was the Kushite seat. Tefnakht details come from the stela translation only.
